```{r setup}
res <- file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "results")
fits <- read.csv(file.path(res, "fits.csv"))
paired <- read.csv(file.path(res, "paired.csv"))
per_call <- read.csv(file.path(res, "controls-per-call.csv"))
pure_r <- read.csv(file.path(res, "controls-pure-r.csv"))
replay <- read.csv(file.path(res, "controls-replay.csv"))
starts <- readRDS(file.path(res, "starts.rds"))
env <- readRDS(file.path(res, "environment.rds"))
case_lab <- c(opaka = "Opakapaka", io_yft = "IO yellowfin (AGE-SF)")
f1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
jit <- paired[paired$start_id > 0, ]
```

## Question

R 4.6.2's NEWS lists one change to `nlminb()`:

> Fix long standing (Fortran compiler optimization related) bug in nlminb with
> constraints, thanks to Kasper Kristensen's PR#19086 report and patch.

The entry does not mention speed. This note checks whether opal fits with
bounds run faster, take a different path, or reach different optima under
R 4.6.2 than under R 4.5.2, the version in opal's `renv.lock`, and whether
any difference comes from the fix or from the compiler used to build R.

## Setup

```{r env-table}
knitr::kable(env, col.names = c("", "R 4.5.2", "R 4.6.2"))
```

* Both R versions are conda-forge builds, run on one cloud
  container (`r env$value_452[env$item == "CPU"]`, 4 cores). conda-forge has no
  R packages built for 4.6 yet, so every package in the 4.6.2 library was built
  from source at the version in the 4.5.2 library (`setup-r462.sh`); RTMB,
  RTMBdist, StanEstimators, SparseNUTS and opal (`dev` at `87c5494`) were
  built from the same source in both.
* Models: the Opakapaka quickstart fit
  (`r starts$opaka$n_par` parameters) and the IO yellowfin article model
  AGE-SF (`r starts$io_yft$n_par` parameters), rebuilt from the fits stored in
  opal's `inst/extdata` with the stored bounds and `nlminb` control
  (`eval.max = iter.max = 10000`). All parameters have finite bounds.
* Fits: two `nlminb` passes with bounds, as in `opal_fit()`. Start 0 is the
  stored model's initial values; starts 1 to N are jittered from the stored
  estimate. Calls to `fn` and `gr` are counted with the wrapper from opal's
  `helper-benchmark.R`.
* Jitter: the SS3 3.30 scheme with a jitter fraction of
  `r starts$opaka$jf` on every parameter. Draws whose objective or gradient
  was not finite (nlminb stops at once on those) were redrawn:
  `r starts$opaka$rejected` for Opakapaka and `r starts$io_yft$rejected` for
  IO yellowfin. Both R versions used the same starts.
* Timing: each fit runs in a fresh R process, one at a time, single-threaded
  BLAS. The order of the two R versions alternates from start to start. Each
  fit is repeated in its process (`r fits$reps[fits$case == "opaka"][1]`
  times for Opakapaka, `r fits$reps[fits$case == "io_yft"][1]` for IO
  yellowfin) and the median time of the `nlminb` calls is reported.

## Controls

Before attributing any difference to `nlminb`, the model's arithmetic must be
the same under both versions.

```{r replay}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Check = c(paste("Stored trajectory replay,", replay$model),
                       paste("Objective and gradient at the jittered starts,", case_lab[unique(paired$case)])),
             `Compared` = c(paste(replay$events, "calls"),
                            paste(as.vector(table(paired$case)[unique(paired$case)]), "starts (fn and gr)")),
             `Identical (fraction)` = c(replay$identical_between_versions,
                                        tapply(paired$same_start_fn & paired$same_start_gr,
                                               paired$case, mean)[unique(paired$case)]),
             check.names = FALSE),
  digits = 3)
```

The trajectory replay uses opal's stored benchmark trajectories
(`tests/testthat/_benchmark/trajectories`; Opakapaka quickstart and the
bundled IO yellowfin LEN inputs), sampled to at most 100 `fn` and 100 `gr`
calls each.

```{r per-call}
pc <- reshape(per_call, idvar = "case", timevar = "r_version", direction = "wide")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model = case_lab[pc$case],
                        `fn, R 4.5.2 (ms)` = 1000 * pc$`fn_s.R 4.5.2`,
                        `fn, R 4.6.2 (ms)` = 1000 * pc$`fn_s.R 4.6.2`,
                        `gr, R 4.5.2 (ms)` = 1000 * pc$`gr_s.R 4.5.2`,
                        `gr, R 4.6.2 (ms)` = 1000 * pc$`gr_s.R 4.6.2`,
                        check.names = FALSE), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Time per objective and gradient call at the estimate (median of 5 blocks).")
```

```{r pure-r}
knitr::kable(pure_r[, c("problem", "r_version", "seconds", "iterations", "fn_evals",
                        "gr_evals", "objective")],
             digits = c(0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 6),
             caption = "nlminb on a 200-parameter extended Rosenbrock function in plain R (no opal); bounded: all parameters in [-1.5, 0.8]. Time is the mean of 20 runs.")
```

## Results

```{r summary-table}
summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(jit, jit$case), function(d) data.frame(
  Model = case_lab[d$case[1]], Starts = nrow(d),
  `Median time 4.5.2 (s)` = median(d$elapsed_452),
  `Median time 4.6.2 (s)` = median(d$elapsed_462),
  `Median ratio 4.6.2/4.5.2` = median(d$time_ratio),
  `Same fn/gr counts` = sum(d$fn_evals_452 == d$fn_evals_462 & d$gr_evals_452 == d$gr_evals_462),
  `Median gr calls 4.5.2` = median(d$gr_evals_452),
  `Median gr calls 4.6.2` = median(d$gr_evals_462),
  `Same end point (|objective difference| < 1e-4)` = sum(abs(d$obj_462 - d$obj_452) < 1e-4, na.rm = TRUE),
  `Total time 4.5.2 (s)` = sum(d$elapsed_452),
  `Total time 4.6.2 (s)` = sum(d$elapsed_462),
  check.names = FALSE)))
knitr::kable(summ, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Jittered starts (start 0 excluded).")
```

```{r same-end}
same <- jit[abs(jit$obj_462 - jit$obj_452) < 1e-4, ]
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(same, same$case), function(d) data.frame(
  Model = case_lab[d$case[1]], Starts = nrow(d),
  `Median time 4.5.2 (s)` = median(d$elapsed_452),
  `Median time 4.6.2 (s)` = median(d$elapsed_462),
  `Median gr calls 4.5.2` = median(d$gr_evals_452),
  `Median gr calls 4.6.2` = median(d$gr_evals_462), check.names = FALSE))),
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Jittered starts where both versions reached the same end point, so the work compared is for the same result.")
```

```{r fig-time, fig.cap = "Time per fit (median of repeats) for each start, R 4.6.2 against R 4.5.2, log scales. The line is equal time; grey is start 0."}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (cs in unique(paired$case)) {
  d <- paired[paired$case == cs, ]
  lim <- range(c(d$elapsed_452, d$elapsed_462))
  plot(d$elapsed_452, d$elapsed_462, xlim = lim, ylim = lim, pch = 19, log = "xy",
       col = ifelse(d$start_id == 0, "grey50", "black"),
       xlab = "R 4.5.2 (s)", ylab = "R 4.6.2 (s)", main = case_lab[cs], cex.main = 0.9)
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
}
par(op)
```

```{r fig-evals, fig.cap = "Gradient calls per fit, R 4.6.2 against R 4.5.2, log scales."}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (cs in unique(paired$case)) {
  d <- paired[paired$case == cs, ]
  lim <- range(c(d$gr_evals_452, d$gr_evals_462))
  plot(d$gr_evals_452, d$gr_evals_462, xlim = lim, ylim = lim, pch = 19, log = "xy",
       xlab = "R 4.5.2", ylab = "R 4.6.2", main = case_lab[cs], cex.main = 0.9)
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
}
par(op)
```

```{r fig-obj, fig.cap = "Final objective minus the stored estimate's objective, per start. Values below 0 are lower than the stored fit."}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (cs in unique(paired$case)) {
  d <- paired[paired$case == cs, ]
  y <- cbind(d$dobj_mle_452, d$dobj_mle_462)
  matplot(d$start_id, y, pch = c(1, 4), col = 1, xlab = "Start", ylab = "Objective - stored",
          main = case_lab[cs], cex.main = 0.9)
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  legend("center", c("R 4.5.2", "R 4.6.2"), pch = c(1, 4), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}
par(op)
```

```{r per-start}
show <- paired[, c("case", "start_id", "elapsed_452", "elapsed_462", "gr_evals_452",
                   "gr_evals_462", "conv_452", "conv_462", "dobj_mle_452", "dobj_mle_462",
                   "max_abs_par_diff")]
names(show) <- c("Model", "Start", "Time 4.5.2", "Time 4.6.2", "gr 4.5.2", "gr 4.6.2",
                 "Conv 4.5.2", "Conv 4.6.2", "dObj 4.5.2", "dObj 4.6.2", "Max |par diff|")
show$Model <- case_lab[show$Model]
knitr::kable(show, digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 6), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Every fit. Time in seconds; dObj is the final objective minus the stored estimate's objective; the last column compares the two versions' final parameters.")
```

## Same-compiler test

```{r sc-load}
sc <- file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "same-compiler", "results")
vr <- read.csv(file.path(sc, "variants.csv"))
mt <- read.csv(file.path(sc, "match.csv"))
ro <- read.csv(file.path(sc, "rosen.csv"))
vlab <- c(A = "A: old code, GCC 10.4, -O2", B = "B: old code, GCC 15.3, -O2",
          C = "C: fixed code, GCC 10.4, -O2", D = "D: fixed code, GCC 15.3, -O2",
          E = "E: old code, GCC 10.4, -O0")
```

The two R builds differ in both the PORT code and the compiler. To separate
the two, R's PORT source (`src/library/stats/src/port.c` and `portsrc.f`) was
taken from the R 4.5.2 and R 4.6.2 tags of the R source mirror on GitHub and
compiled into five standalone libraries (`same-compiler/build-port-variants.sh`).
The only change to `portsrc.f` between the two tags is the fix:

```fortran
-         CALL DL7TVM(N, V(X01), V(L), V(X01))
-         CALL DL7VML(N, V(X01), V(L), V(X01))
+         TEMP1 = IV(STLSTG)
+         CALL DL7TVM(N, V(TEMP1), V(L), V(X01))
+         CALL DL7VML(N, V(X01), V(L), V(TEMP1))
```

In the old code the same array is passed as both input and output of
`DL7TVM` and `DL7VML`. Fortran does not allow this, so an optimising compiler
may produce code whose result differs from the one the authors intended. The
fix passes a separate work vector.

`portsrc.f` was compiled with the same flags as R's builds (`SAFE_FFLAGS`), by
the same conda-forge compilers that built each R version's `stats` library;
`port.c` (C glue, no change of substance between the tags) was compiled with
GCC 15.3 in every variant. Each library was loaded into R 4.6.2 behind a copy
of R 4.6.2's `nlminb()`, so R, BLAS, the model and the starts are the same for
every variant.

```{r sc-match}
mt$Variant <- vlab[mt$variant]
mt$Model <- case_lab[mt$case]
knitr::kable(mt[, c("Model", "Variant", "starts", "same_as_r452", "same_as_r462")],
             col.names = c("Model", "Variant", "Fits",
                           "Identical to R 4.5.2", "Identical to R 4.6.2"),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Fits (start 0 and the jittered starts) whose objective and gradient call counts and final objective are identical to those of stats::nlminb in R 4.5.2 or R 4.6.2 (main benchmark).")
```

```{r sc-rosen}
rb <- ro[ro$problem == "bounded", ]
rb$variant <- ifelse(rb$variant == "stats", "stats::nlminb (R 4.6.2)", vlab[rb$variant])
knitr::kable(rb[, c("variant", "iterations", "fn_evals", "gr_evals", "objective")],
             col.names = c("Variant", "Iterations", "fn calls", "gr calls", "Objective"),
             row.names = FALSE, digits = 6,
             caption = "Bounded Rosenbrock problem (plain R) with each variant. Without bounds all variants take the same path (730 iterations).")
```

```{r sc-summary}
vs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(vr[vr$start_id > 0, ], list(vr$case[vr$start_id > 0], vr$variant[vr$start_id > 0])), function(d)
  data.frame(Model = case_lab[d$case[1]], Variant = vlab[d$variant[1]],
             `Median gr calls` = median(d$gr_evals),
             `Median time (s)` = median(d$elapsed_s),
             `Total time (s)` = sum(d$elapsed_s), check.names = FALSE)))
vs <- vs[order(vs$Model, vs$Variant), ]
knitr::kable(vs, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Jittered starts by variant, all run in R 4.6.2 (times: median of 3 repeats for Opakapaka, 1 run for IO yellowfin).")
```

Results:

* **The compiler version had no effect** between GCC 10.4 and 15.3. A and B (old code)
  give identical results to each other and to R 4.5.2 at every fit; C and D
  (fixed code) give identical results to each other and to R 4.6.2.
* **The code change accounts for every difference** between R 4.5.2 and R 4.6.2
  in this benchmark, including the evaluation counts, the end points and the
  plain-R problem.
* **Optimisation is what triggers the bug.** The old code compiled without
  optimisation (E, `-O0`) gives results identical to the fixed code at every
  fit. Compiled at `-O2` by either compiler, the old code computes a different
  result. The agreement of E with the fixed code indicates that the fixed code
  computes what the old code was written to compute, and that the optimised
  builds of the old code (R 4.5.2 here) did not.

## Interpretation

```{r interp-numbers}
op <- jit[jit$case == "opaka", ]
io <- jit[jit$case == "io_yft", ]
mins <- sort(unique(round(c(op$obj_452, op$obj_462), 3)))
low <- min(c(op$obj_452, op$obj_462))
n_low <- c(sum(op$obj_452 - low < 1e-4), sum(op$obj_462 - low < 1e-4))
io_diff <- abs(io$obj_462 - io$obj_452) >= 1e-4
pr <- pure_r[pure_r$problem == "bounded", ]
pu <- pure_r[pure_r$problem == "unbounded", ]
```

**Model arithmetic.** Both builds return identical objective and gradient
values in the trajectory replay and at every start. The cost per call differs
by 13% or less between versions, and not consistently in one direction. The
differences below therefore come from the path `nlminb` takes, not from the
model.

**Opakapaka.** R 4.6.2 used fewer gradient calls at all
`r nrow(op)` jittered starts (median `r median(op$gr_evals_462)` against
`r median(op$gr_evals_452)`) and took a median `r f2(median(op$time_ratio))`
of R 4.5.2's time. The fits ended at one of two minima,
`r mins[1]` and `r mins[2]`; the stored quickstart estimate is the higher
one. R 4.5.2 reached the lower minimum from `r n_low[1]` starts and R 4.6.2
from `r n_low[2]`; the `r sum(abs(op$obj_462 - op$obj_452) >= 1e-4)` starts
where the versions disagree all ended lower under R 4.5.2. Fewer evaluations
did not mean a better end point here.

**IO yellowfin.** R 4.6.2 used fewer gradient calls at
`r sum(io$gr_evals_462 < io$gr_evals_452)` of `r nrow(io)` starts; the median
time ratio was `r f2(median(io$time_ratio))` (range
`r f2(min(io$time_ratio))` to `r f2(max(io$time_ratio))`). The total time is
dominated by start 5, where R 4.5.2 reached the evaluation limit
(`r io$gr_evals_452[io$start_id == 5]` gradient calls) and R 4.6.2 stopped
after `r io$gr_evals_462[io$start_id == 5]` with false convergence. Only
`r sum(io$dobj_mle_452 < 1e-3)` jittered start returned to the stored
estimate under either version; with a jitter fraction of 0.1 this
`r starts$io_yft$n_par`-parameter model mostly ends in worse local minima.
The two versions ended at different points from `r sum(io_diff)` starts
(R 4.6.2 lower at `r sum(io$obj_462 < io$obj_452 - 1e-4)`, higher at
`r sum(io$obj_462 > io$obj_452 + 1e-4)`), so for this model most time
comparisons are between fits that did not reach the same result. At the
`r sum(!io_diff)` starts where they did, R 4.6.2 was faster (table above).

**Plain-R problem.** Without bounds, both versions took the same path
(`r pu$iterations[1]` iterations). With bounds, R 4.6.2 needed more
iterations (`r pr$iterations[pr$r_version == "R 4.6.2"]` against
`r pr$iterations[pr$r_version == "R 4.5.2"]`) and more time, for the same
solution. In this example only the bounded run changed, in line with the NEWS
entry, and R 4.6.2 did more work, not less.

**Inference.** The same-compiler test shows that the differences between
R 4.5.2 and R 4.6.2 come from the `nlminb` fix, not from the compiler. Whenever
the old `portsrc.f` was compiled with optimisation (`-O2`, either GCC), it took
a different path from the unoptimised old code and the fixed code. For these two opal models, the intended
path (R 4.6.2) needed fewer evaluations and less time at most jittered starts;
for the plain-R problem it needed more. Neither version reached better end
points consistently. The samples are small, so the size of the speed-up for
other models cannot be inferred from these results.

## Limitations

* conda-forge built R 4.5.2's `stats` library (which holds `nlminb`'s PORT
  code) with `r env$value_452[env$item == "stats.so built with"]` and
  R 4.6.2's with `r env$value_462[env$item == "stats.so built with"]`. The
  same-compiler test separates the code change from this compiler change for
  these two GCC versions at `-O0` and `-O2` only. Other compilers and flags
  (e.g. the gfortran builds used for CRAN's Windows and macOS R, or `-O3`)
  were not tested, so whether a given R < 4.6.2 installation shows the old
  behaviour has to be checked on that installation. One machine was used.
* In the same-compiler test, `port.c` was compiled with GCC 15.3 in every
  variant (R 4.6's headers need C23 support that GCC 10 lacks). Variants A and
  B still reproduce R 4.5.2's results exactly, so this did not affect them.
* Small samples: `r nrow(jit[jit$case == "opaka", ])` and
  `r nrow(jit[jit$case == "io_yft", ])` jittered starts. The jitter draws were
  limited to starts with a finite objective and gradient.
* Timings come from a shared cloud container. Alternating the order of the
  versions and repeating each fit reduce, but do not remove, drift and noise.
* Packages in the 4.5.2 library are conda-forge binaries; in the 4.6.2 library
  they were compiled here from the same versions. The controls above check
  that the model's arithmetic agrees; they cannot rule out differences in
  code paths that the controls do not exercise.
* Two packages differ from the 4.5.2 library: checkmate is 2.3.4 in R 4.6.2
  (2.3.3 does not compile against R 4.6) and bibtex is added (needed to build
  mvtnorm). Neither is used in the model calculations.
* Only `nlminb()` with opal's default control settings was tested.

## Reproduce

```bash
OPAL_SOURCE=/path/to/opal bash benchmarks/nlminb-r46/setup-r452.sh
bash benchmarks/nlminb-r46/setup-r462.sh /opt/r452 $HOME/r-setup-r452/src
OPAL_SOURCE=/path/to/opal bash benchmarks/nlminb-r46/run-benchmark.sh
bash benchmarks/nlminb-r46/same-compiler/run-same-compiler.sh
quarto render benchmarks/nlminb-r46/nlminb-r46.qmd
```
